features.name: Portfolio Diversification Index
features.description: Measures the average pairwise correlation between stocks in the portfolio using equal weights. Lower values indicate better diversification.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate pairwise Pearson correlations between all companies' returns over a 60-day rolling window.
Average the correlation matrix values across all pairs to produce a single portfolio-level metric.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater correlation between stocks (lower diversification), lower values indicate more分散的 returns across the portfolio.

features.name: Market Leadership Concentration Score
features.description: Measures the fraction of total portfolio return contributed by the top-performing companies in a rolling window.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
For each day, rank companies by their 20-day trailing return.
Sum the absolute values of returns from the top 10% of companies and divide by total portfolio return (using equal weights).
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate that a small subset of stocks drives most of the portfolio's performance, lower values suggest more distributed leadership.

features.name: Momentum Shift Frequency
features.description: Counts the number of times the portfolio transitions between positive and negative momentum regimes in a rolling window.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 5-day trailing cumulative return for equal-weighted portfolio.
Count the number of sign changes in the momentum signal over a 20-day rolling window.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more frequent regime shifts in portfolio momentum behavior.

features.name: Volatility Regime Stability
features.description: Measures the consistency of volatility clustering patterns using rolling standard deviation of returns.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 20-day rolling standard deviation of equal-weighted portfolio returns.
Count the number of times volatility crosses above/below a 60-day moving average threshold.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more frequent and unstable volatility regime transitions.

features.name: Portfolio Regime Transition Frequency
features.description: Counts the number of transitions between bull, bear, and sideways market states based on equal-weighted returns.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Define bull state as 20-day return > 1%, bear state as < -1%, sideways otherwise.
Count transitions between states in a 60-day rolling window.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater frequency of regime changes in portfolio performance patterns.

features.name: Systematic Risk Amplification Index
features.description: Measures the average correlation between individual stock returns and equal-weighted portfolio returns.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 20-day rolling correlation between each stock's return and the equal-weighted portfolio return.
Average these correlations across all companies to produce a single metric.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater alignment with systemic market factors (higher systematic risk amplification).

features.name: Recovery Velocity Index
features.description: Measures the time taken to recover from drawdowns relative to historical benchmarks.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Identify drawdown periods (portfolio return < previous peak).
Calculate the number of days required to recover to previous peak level.
Average recovery times across all identified drawdown events.
features.interpretation: Lower values indicate faster recovery from drawdowns (higher resilience).

features.name: Liquidity Correlation Intensity
features.description: Measures the average pairwise correlation between stocks' dollar volumes (close × volume).
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily dollar volume for each company as close × volume.
Calculate 20-day rolling standard deviation of dollar volume for each company.
Calculate pairwise Pearson correlations between all companies' dollar volume volatility.
Average these correlations across all pairs to produce a single metric.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater synchronization in liquidity risk across portfolio stocks.

features.name: Sentiment Coherence Score
features.description: Measures the correlation between equal-weighted portfolio returns and cross-sectional standard deviation of individual stock returns.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 20-day rolling standard deviation of individual stock returns (cross-sectionally).
Calculate 20-day rolling correlation between portfolio return and cross-sectional standard deviation.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Higher positive values indicate stronger alignment between portfolio returns and market-wide dispersion patterns.

features.name: Risk Contribution Uniformity Index
features.description: Measures the standard deviation of individual stock volatilities in the equal-weighted portfolio.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 20-day rolling standard deviation of returns for each company.
Compute cross-sectional standard deviation of these individual volatilities across the portfolio.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more uniform risk contribution across stocks (better diversification).

features.name: Portfolio Regime Adaptability Index
features.description: Measures the coefficient of variation of portfolio returns during different volatility regimes.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Define high/low volatility states based on 60-day rolling standard deviation thresholds.
Calculate coefficient of variation (standard deviation/mean) of portfolio returns in each regime.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more consistent performance across different volatility regimes.

features.name: Information Flow Dominance Metric
features.description: Measures the R-squared of portfolio returns regressed against trading volume changes.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 5-day change in trading volume (volume - lagged volume) for each company.
Perform linear regression of portfolio return on volume changes across all companies.
Return the R-squared value from this regression.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater proportion of price movements explained by trading volume changes (information flow).

features.name: Dynamic Correlation Stability
features.description: Measures the standard deviation of pairwise stock correlations over time.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 20-day rolling Pearson correlations between all pairs of stocks.
Compute cross-sectional standard deviation of these correlation values across the portfolio.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more stable inter-stock relationships over time.

features.name: Tail Risk Exposure Concentration
features.description: Measures the cross-sectional standard deviation of returns during extreme downside events.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Identify days where portfolio return is in the bottom 10% of historical values.
Calculate cross-sectional standard deviation of individual stock returns on these tail risk days.
Return null if fewer than 80% of required observations are available.
features.interpretation: Lower values indicate more diversified tail risk exposure across the portfolio.

features.name: Portfolio Entropy of Returns
features.description: Measures the Shannon entropy of the equal-weighted portfolio return distribution.
procedure: Sort data by company and date.
Compute daily returns for each company using div_adj_close.
Calculate 60-day rolling equal-weighted portfolio returns.
Estimate probability distribution of these returns using kernel density estimation.
Compute Shannon entropy from this distribution.
features.interpretation: Higher values indicate more unpredictable/chaotic return patterns, lower values suggest structured behavior.
